notes:
Summary: Large enterprise search vendor evaluating Redwood for a massive-scale vector index (targeting 200M-800M vectors). Primary goal: reduce per-query unit cost while meeting tight reranking latency targets.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-01-20: Intro call (Elena + Ravi) — client described current infra: custom vector store on k8s + hybrid HDFS, heavy operational overhead.
- 2026-01-28: Architecture deep-dive (SE) — discussed sharding, multi-tier storage, quantization approaches.
- 2026-02-10: Kickoff POC scoping (Fireflies: FF-20260210-ASW-kickoff) — agreed on dataset sample (1.2B docs -> will sample ~300M vectors for POC).
- 2026-02-24: Security & compliance sync (Priya present) — requested SOC2 + ISO27001 evidence; asked for KMS integration options. (Fireflies: FF-20260224-ASW-arch-review)
- 2026-02-28: Internal ops call — client agrees to fund 1-week Dedicated POC if cost-per-query estimates provided up front.

Use-case & requirements (from calls / notes):
- Workload: enterprise RAG + semantic search front-end; heavy reranking step after ANN retrieval.
- Scale: target index size 200M-800M vectors in first phase; roadmap to 1B+.
- Latency targets: 95th pctile rerank < 80ms (prefer sub-50ms for hot queries). Initial kNN recall target: P@10 > 0.85.
- Throughput: baseline 300 QPS sustained during business hours, spikes to 2k QPS for batch jobs / reindex windows.
- Cost sensitivity: high — unit economics must beat current on-prem spend; client uses cost-per-query and $/million tokens as decision metrics.
- Model preferences: open quantized embeddings (multi-dim 1024 preferred) + ability to run smaller dense reranker models co-located to reduce cross-network hops.
- Indexing strategy wanted: hybrid storage (NVMe for hot shards, cheaper object store for warm), aggressive PQ/IVF or OPQ+Q4_0 for storage reduction.
- Caching & batching: need prefix/KV cache for chat sessions + request-level batching for embedding creation. Expect Redwood Optimize recommendations to be useful.
- Routing/fallbacks: multi-variant routing (high-precision model route vs cheap fallback) for cost control.

Security / compliance notes:
- Must pass SSO/SAML integration and demonstrate audit logs to meet SOC2 audit.
- Data residency: require EU and NA residency controls per dataset; initial POC will keep NA only.
- KMS: customer uses on-prem HSM; needs key wrapping options.

POC scope & success criteria:
- Index 300M sampled vectors into Redwood Dedicated cluster (gov-like VPC) and run 2 live queries workloads: search + rerank.
- Measure: avg cost/query, 95th latency for reranker, throughput under 300/2k QPS, index build time, and storage footprint.
- Acceptance: rerank 95th < 80ms AND unit cost < current infra cost baseline.

Quotes / call snippets:
- "If we can't hit sub-80ms for rerank at scale, it's a non-starter." — Head of Search Eng
- "We need transparent cost breakdowns per token/query; no black box." — Procurement

Open items / asks for Redwood team:
- Detailed cost model for Dedicated + Private options including storage tiering assumptions.
- Proof-of-concept runbook and minimal infra spec for POC (GPU types, network, storage sizing).
- Security pack: SOC2 cert, ISO docs, KMS integration playbook, sample audit log entries.
- Engineering checklist: acceptance tests for KV cache correctness and batching behavior.

Next steps (short):
- SE (Ravi) to deliver POC infra spec and cost estimate by 2026-03-05.
- Legal to share draft SLA for on-prem/private by 2026-03-12.
- Set up Dedicated POC environment once budget approved (target week of 2026-03-22).

Internal notes:
- Strong opportunity to sell Dedicated -> Private path; upsell Optimize for quantization and batching tuning.
- Competitive pressure from Pinecone and internal open-source infra; emphasize operational simplicity and unified routing/fallbacks.
- Watch for procurement timeline slippage — budget approval is the riskiest blocker.
